title: An illustration Ask draws looks illustrated: natural shapes, light and shadow, depth
goal: When a person asks for an illustration (a sun over mountains, a landscape, an animal), Ask draws it the way an illustrator would: natural outlines instead of plain triangles and circles, a light side and a shadow side that agree with where the light comes from, soft gradients, and depth from layers that fade into the distance. An icon request stays simple and bold; an illustration request gets the craft.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-20 11:32 (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-sun-over-mountains.png): 'the sun over mountains test produces such bad results. mountains aren't triangles, they are natural shapes with shadowing and such. I think if you're drawing an svg illustration of sun over mountains it should be more elaborate.' The picture: a flat yellow circle, two flat green triangles and a third green wedge clipped by the box on the right, no shading, no sky.

Waits on ask-draws-a-dog-you-can-tell-is-a-dog (in progress, going the one-SVG-per-drawing route with Twemoji as a built-in set and llama3.2-vision to look). Twemoji-style flat art is right for icons and emoji-like requests but is not this bar. Paint has linear and radial gradients (Sources/PhotonzCore/Paint.swift). Ways in, decide and log: an illustration brief in the prompt (light direction, value layers, ridge noise), a two-pass draw (forms first, then a light pass that adds shadow faces), and the look-and-revise loop judged on crafted. Rubric: Scripts/ask-eval/rubric.md.

The user, 2026-10-20 11:33, with a board of sun-over-mountains SVGs from a web image search (Etsy, PremiumSVG, Vecteezy, FreePixel; saved as queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-sun-mountains-reference-board.png): 'if you search for examples, you'll find a wide variety. it may be interesting to explore how we create things at this quality'. Those are other people's paid or licensed artwork: study the techniques, never trace, copy or ship any of them. Masks and clipping exist in the app (a layer used as a mask); check the agent tools reach them.
acceptance: 'draw an svg illustration of a sun over mountains' on a blank picture gives mountains with irregular ridgelines and curves (no straight-sided triangles), each with a lit face and a shadow face that agree with where the sun is, at least three ranges that get lighter and bluer into the distance, a sky gradient, and nothing poking past the picture by accident (the user's result had a stray green wedge off the right edge)

The quality bar is the user's reference board (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-sun-mountains-reference-board.png): before building, the runner studies how those pieces are made and writes the techniques into the audit, at least: silhouettes with snow and ridge highlights cut as negative space, sun rays as an even radial burst, a scene clipped into a circle or badge with a frame line, repeated pine silhouettes for a treeline, lake reflections as stacked horizontal strokes, and layered sunset ridges stepping in value under a gradient sky

Ask follows the style the person names: 'line art', 'silhouette', 'badge' or 'circle', 'sunset', 'flat' each give that look, and with no style named it picks one and the row says which. The eval gets one case per style (sun over mountains as line art, as a black silhouette badge with pines, as a layered sunset), each scoring 7 or more on crafted and designed, and a judge shown the board says the result belongs among them

Techniques become reusable pieces Ask can call (for example a treeline, a ray burst, a ridge with a shadow face, a clip to a circle), so a drawing is composed rather than written point by point; which ones is the runner's call, logged

The eval's rubric gets a 'crafted' line for illustrations (natural forms, light and shadow, depth, finish), and the user's picture (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-sun-over-mountains.png) scores 3 or lower on it

Five illustration cases in the eval (sun over mountains, a forest at dusk, a lighthouse on a cliff, a fox, a city skyline at night) reach 7 or more on crafted and designed for Ask on this Mac, before and after in the audit; the thirteen drawing cases of the dog task do not go down
Every part stays editable and named (ridges, shadow faces, sky, sun), uses the app's own gradient fills, and exports as clean SVG

Audit under queue/audits/ with a contact sheet before and after and the scores. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: intake: the user's reference board sets the quality bar; styles by name; techniques as reusable pieces
